Further from Wall Street, he reset US foreign policy by cutting Ukraine off from Starlink — a move that says enough about who’s in charge that President Donald Trump claimed credit for reversing it — and dominated the midterm-elections homestretch with spending that will near $450 million this cycle. After his post-DOGE meltdown last year, many had thought Musk had been neutered. He lost his lawsuit against OpenAI. SpaceX’s grandiose IPO prospectus drew titters from an investment community generally prone to believe outlandish promises. But like X, Musk has emerged stronger and more central to finance, politics, and culture.

stories.summary: A heated debate over how to define what qualifies as an ultra-processed food contributed to the resignation of Trump administration health adviser Calley Means ahead of the midterm elections. People familiar with his exit say he was frustrated with a lack of progress toward the release of a white paper with a proposed definition. Means blamed ultra-processed foods for the “ chronic disease crisis ” in the US. But the food industry has raised concerns over what impact the forthcoming proposed definition could have on lawsuits across the country, and the White House is still scheduled to meet separately with several groups to discuss the issue in the coming weeks — including the National Restaurant Association on Tuesday , the Center for Food Safety on Thursday , and the Consumer Brands Association and Flavor and Extract Manufacturers Association in the days after the midterms. — David Lim

articles.title: Trump administration has pushed off 13% of Americans enrolled in food stamps
articles.author: Eric Berger
articles.summary: Stakeholders concerned more people at risk of food insecurity after One Big Beautiful Act took effect Enrollment in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Snap) has decreased significantly over the past year in the US following restrictions imposed by the Trump administration, which has forced more people to seek help from food banks or go hungry, stakeholders say. The number of people who receive food stamps has dropped from 41.6 million in July 2025, before the One Big Beautiful Act took effect, to 36.5 million in June 2026, a 13% decrease, according to the latest data from the US Department of Agriculture , which administers the program.
